<div class="adr-inshort"><span class="adr-inshort-label">In short</span><p><code>$subject |&gt; Str::trim($_) |&gt; Str::lower($_)</code> — the right side of <code>|&gt;</code> is an ordinary expression containing the hole <code>$_</code> <strong>exactly once</strong>, and the operator replaces that hole with the left side <strong>in the parser</strong>. The result is the same AST the nested spelling produces, so every later pass — name resolution, the type checker, taint and <code>secret</code>, <a href="/docs/adr/0057/" data-adr="0057">0057</a>'s literal folding, IR lowering, codegen — sees a node it already handles and none of them changes. This is deliberately <strong>not</strong> PHP 8.5's <code>|&gt;</code>, which applies a unary <em>callable</em> resolved at run time: that design needs free functions Novis does not have (<a href="/docs/adr/0011/" data-adr="0011">0011</a>), callable spellings Novis closed (<a href="/docs/adr/0027/" data-adr="0027">0027</a>), and a closure wrapper at nearly every <code>Core</code> call site because R2 puts an options bag on most members. The shared spelling is kept and the PHP <em>shape</em> is rejected by name, which is the same move <a href="/docs/adr/0034/" data-adr="0034">0034</a>, <a href="/docs/adr/0045/" data-adr="0045">0045</a> and <a href="/docs/adr/0050/" data-adr="0050">0050</a> already make.</p></div>

<a class="adr-source-link" href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0098.md">View the source of this decision on GitHub</a>

## Context

- **The cost being removed is reading order, not name length.** `Core` members compose by nesting, and a
  three-deep composition reads inside-out: `tests/conformance/core/arr-map-and-filter-keep-their-keys.nvst`
  writes `Core\Str::join(Core\Arr::values(Core\Arr::map($kept, fn(int $n) => $n as string)), ",")`, and
  `examples/text.nvs` and `examples/numbers.nvs` each carry two more. A `use`-shorthand for `Core` members
  — floated in [0011](/docs/adr/0011/) § *Revisiting* — shortens the
  names and leaves the order exactly as it was.
- **The obvious fix is forbidden and should stay forbidden.** Methods on scalars (`$s->trim()`) is what
  [0063](/docs/adr/0063/) R19 exists to prevent, and R19 is load-bearing: 0063's own
  *Consequences* names *"a reviewer reads authority off the call site — `Path::` cannot touch the disk,
  `IO::` can"*. A fluent method deletes the class name, which is the token carrying that signal. An
  operator keeps it at every step.
- **R1 is not what makes this work, and that matters.** *"The subject is parameter 1, always"* would let a
  first-argument-insertion pipe (Elixir's, Gleam's) be always-correct for `Core`, but it is not correct for
  userland, which R1 does not bind, and it cannot reach `Arr::contains($haystack, $needle)`'s second slot.
  A hole depends on no convention at all.
- **The field has converged on the hole.** `|>` carries three different meanings across the languages that
  have it — unary application (F#, OCaml, Elm, Julia, PHP 8.5), first-argument insertion (Elixir, Gleam),
  and hole substitution (Hack's `$$`, R's `_`, the JavaScript proposal's `%`). TC39 evaluated the first
  against the third and chose the third, for the reason that decides it here too: real functions are not
  unary.
- **PHP 8.5 ships `|>` and it is a different operator.** Verified against the 8.5.9 oracle this repository
  pins: the right side is a callable value invoked with one argument, so `"a-b-c" |> (fn($s) =>
  str_replace("-", "+", $s))` needs the closure, an unparenthesized arrow function is a dedicated fatal
  error, a non-callable right side is a **run-time** `Error` rather than a compile error, and
  `$f = "strtoupper"; "q" |> $f` resolves by name at run time. The last of those is a spelling
  [0027](/docs/adr/0027/) already removed.

## Decision

**`|>` is a binary operator whose right side is an expression containing `$_` exactly once. The parser
replaces that hole with the left side and emits the resulting expression. There is no run-time
representation of `|>`, and no callable is involved.**

### 1. The one rule

```
PipeExpr := Unary ( "|>" PipeRhs )*
PipeRhs  := Postfix                     // a call, an index, a member access, or a parenthesized group
```

`$subject |> RHS` produces `RHS` with its `$_` replaced by `$subject`. Left-associative, so
`$a |> f($_) |> g($_)` is `g(f($a))`.

The right side is parsed at the postfix level, so an expression that is not already a call or an access is
written parenthesized: `$n |> ($_ * 2)`. This is one stated rule rather than a precedence puzzle, and it is
what keeps `$a |> Str::upper($_) . "!"` grouping as `Str::upper($a) . "!"` — the trap that makes PHP's
version require parentheses cannot arise here, because substitution of a single hole commutes with the
surrounding operator.

### 2. Precedence

`|>` binds **tighter than every binary operator and looser than unary**, inserted between
`parse_multiplicative` and `parse_not` in [`nvs_syntax::parser::expr`](https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-syntax/src/parser/expr.rs)'s
chain. The four cases this fixes, each of which a looser placement gets wrong:

| written | groups as |
|---|---|
| `-$a \|> Math::abs($_)` | `Math::abs(-$a)` |
| `"x=" . $a \|> Str::upper($_)` | `"x=" . Str::upper($a)` |
| `$a \|> Str::length($_) > 5` | `Str::length($a) > 5` |
| `$x = $a \|> Str::trim($_)` | `$x = Str::trim($a)` |

### 3. The hole is `$_`

`$_` is free for a reason already written down: `nvs_syntax::casing` rejects an identifier made entirely of
underscores, naming PHP's conventional `$_` where it does it, under
[0030](/docs/adr/0030/). The parser turns `$_` into its own node before
casing sees a variable, so nothing there changes.

It wears a `$` because it **is** a binding, and in Novis a binding wears a `$`. Hack's `$$` was rejected for
this slot: `$$name` is PHP's variable-variable spelling, which Novis refuses with a named diagnostic, and
reusing the token for something unrelated is the collision this repository does not make.

### 4. Three diagnostics, in the parser band

| code | when | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| `E0124` | the right side of `\|>` contains no `$_` | *the right side of `\|>` needs the hole `$_` — write `Str::trim($_)`*. **When the right side is first-class callable syntax** (`Foo::bar(...)`) or a closure value, it adds: *PHP 8.5's `\|>` applies a callable; Novis's substitutes `$_`* |
| `E0125` | `$_` appears more than once on one right side | *`$_` may appear exactly once — bind the value to a local instead* |
| `E0126` | `$_` appears outside the right side of a `\|>` | *`$_` is the pipeline hole and has no meaning here* |

`E0124`'s second half is what makes the shared spelling with PHP affordable: the habit is caught at compile
time, at the character where it goes wrong, and named. Exactly one hole is required rather than at least
one, and that is what makes § 1 a substitution with no temporary and no double evaluation — which is in
turn what makes the emitted AST identical to the nested spelling's.

### 5. What this does not change

- **R19 stands.** No scalar and no `array<T>` gains a method. `$s->trim()` is still an error.
- **R17 stands**, and this ADR amends only its wording: an operator is syntax, not a second API, which its
  own table already said of `instanceof`.
- **No `Core` member is added, removed or resigned.** The library is exactly as large as it was.
- **No security property moves.** Taint, `secret`, sinks and launderers
  ([0024](/docs/adr/0024/), [0033](/docs/adr/0033/),
  [0088](/docs/adr/0088/)) run over the substituted AST, so
  `$userTemplate |> Str::format($_, $n)` is refused for the same reason
  `Core\Str::format($userTemplate, $n)` is.
- **No run-time cost.** Identical IR, identical machine code, no closure allocated, no dynamic dispatch.

## Consequences

**Positive**

- A composition reads in the order it runs, and every step still names the class whose authority it uses.
- Userland needs no annotation, no attribute and no registration: the class is written at the call site,
  so resolution is what it already was. A `#[Fluentable]`-style marker — considered and not needed — would
  have made resolution open-world and cost [0061](/docs/adr/0061/)'s
  compile-time determinism.
- It reaches what a fluent method could not: any argument slot, an instance method (`$_->group(1)`), an
  index (`$_["email"]`), a closure in a variable, `new`.
- The implementation is confined to `nvs-syntax`. `ExprKind::StaticCall` is consumed by `nvs-hir`'s
  `members`/`requires`, `nvs-types`' `ctor_init`/`lateinit`/`expr_table` and `nvs-ir`'s `lower::expr`, and
  none of them sees a new node.

**Negative**

- **One more operator on the surface** — priority 4, spent deliberately. It is the whole cost.
- **Two ways to write one composition.** `nvs fmt` canonicalizes neither, by
  [0039](/docs/adr/0039/)'s never-reflow rule. This is a style question a project settles,
  not a correctness one, and it is the reason R17's carve-out had to be made explicit rather than assumed.
- **A shared spelling with PHP that means something else.** `$s |> Str::trim(...)` is valid PHP and an
  error here. Caught at compile time, never silently, by `E0124` — but it is a real divergence on a token
  a PHP developer already knows, and the first one Novis takes rather than rejects outright.
- **A chain through a `?T` is broken today.** R4 makes `?T` returns common, and until *Revisiting*'s `?|>`
  exists such a chain needs an `if` — which is what the deferral is betting is rare enough to wait.

## Alternatives rejected

- **Methods on scalars** (`$s->trim()->upper()`), the JavaScript shape. Rejected on R19, and independently
  on the authority-at-the-call-site argument in *Context*: it erases the class name, needs a scalar-to-`Core`
  map in the checker rather than a parser desugar, has to answer for a `mixed` receiver where `->` already
  means instance access, and gives `nvs fmt` two spellings with no canonical one.
- **PHP 8.5's semantics under the same token.** Rejected in *Context*: it needs `Class::method(...)` as a
  value at every step — a spelling that exists ([0027](/docs/adr/0027/)) but that
  `nvs-ir` does not lower today — and R2's trailing options bag means most `Core` members are not unary, so
  nearly every step would carry a closure wrapper and read worse than the nesting it replaces.
- **First-argument insertion**, no hole (Elixir, Gleam). Terser, and R1 makes it correct for every `Core`
  member. Rejected: it cannot reach a second slot (`Arr::contains($haystack, $needle)`), it makes a call
  expression's arity depend on its context, and R1 does not bind userland, so the rule would have an
  exception the day it shipped.
- **A different token** — `~>`, `->>`, `==>`, each verified free in the lexer. Rejected: `->>` is one glyph
  from `->`, `==>` is one from `=>` and reads as assignment or equality, and `~>` — the only real
  contender — costs the recognition `|>` carries across ten languages while *still* requiring `|>` in the
  lexer as a rejected token to catch the PHP habit. Two tokens and two diagnostics against one and one.
- **`$$` as the hole**, Hack's spelling. Rejected in § 3: it collides with the variable-variable spelling
  Novis refuses by name.
- **A `use function`-style shorthand for `Core` members** ([0011](/docs/adr/0011/)
  § *Revisiting*). Not an alternative to this at all — it shortens names and leaves reading order untouched —
  and it remains open on its own terms.

## Revisiting

- **`?|>`, a null-skipping step**, mirroring `?->`. Deferred, not rejected. The trigger is evidence: the
  remaining Stage 4 conformance and differential cases are the corpus that will show how often a `?T` in
  the middle of a composition forces a chain to be broken. Decide it against that corpus rather than ahead
  of it; a second operator needs a second reason.

## Verification

- **M1**, as this milestone's fifth grammar addition ([docs/plan/m1.md](https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/plan/m1.md)) — and the first of
  the five that blocks no other ADR's scheduled work, which is why it is scheduled after the current loop
  goal rather than into it.
- **M1:** the lexer produces `|>` as one token ahead of `|`, and a unit test asserts that no valid program
  changed meaning — `|` is never followed by `>` in any existing fixture or in the type grammar's unions.
- **M1:** parser tests for the precedence table in § 2, one row each, plus left-associativity over a
  three-step chain.
- **M1:** `tests/conformance/lang/` carries the substitution identity — a `|>` chain and its nested
  spelling produce the same output — over a call, an index, a member access and a parenthesized group.
- **M1:** `tests/conformance/reject/` carries `E0124` in both its forms (a bare right side, and the PHP
  callable shape), `E0125` and `E0126`.
- **M4S:** one differential case proves a `|>` chain over `Core` members agrees with the PHP oracle's
  nested equivalent, which is the same claim the chain's own conformance case makes against a frozen
  output.
